summary: From code: an egress resolve over the overlay has no deadline of its own. scripts/substrate/federation-relay/federation-transport-server.ts resolveOverLibp2p (~753-758) calls resolveViaLibp2p and falls back to resolveViaHttp with no timeout or abort signal, and the library's dial and stream path sets none either (repos/libp2p-federation-transport/src/index.ts ~144-150). The effective bound is whatever each caller happens to set: 240 s for the goal-host proxy, 60 s for the floor tool, 30 s for replication, 20 s for the surface, and none at all for the human-surface passthrough (repos/human-surface-vessel/src/routes/proxy.ts ~646). The transport's own inbound limit (FTS ~504, 120 s) is not coupled to the walk budget either. Effect: a blackholed peer or a stalled stream holds a caller for its own arbitrary bound; on the passthrough it can hang indefinitely; and the time cost of a dead route differs by caller, so it cannot be learned. This is a law-1 constant-by-omission. Expected: one shaped egress deadline, read at use time (for example a field on the existing fedIngressAuthPolicy record or a tuning parameter), applied to the libp2p and HTTP fallback paths, with the inbound limit derived from walkBudget.iter_timeout_ms rather than a literal. A timed-out egress returns a named timeout class, not a generic failure. Fix kind: code, because this is transport plumbing; the deadline value itself becomes a shape. Falsifier: must-fail: an egress resolve to a stub peer that accepts the stream and never answers returns a named egress_timeout within the shaped deadline plus a small slack. Today it waits for the caller's abort, or forever on the passthrough. Control: a peer that answers within the deadline returns its answer unchanged.
falsifier_spec: must-fail: egress to a stub peer that never answers returns a named egress_timeout within the shaped deadline (today waits for caller abort or forever); control: an answering peer is unchanged
